items.text: When an international court and a country's own courts disagree, the international court's ruling should take priority.
items.note: An international court is one set up by agreement between countries, whose rulings cover the countries that join it.
items.rationale: Legal internationalists (monism) endorse; 'human rights' dropped to avoid lib/pro cross-load; frames split on trust in home courts.

items.text: A country's own decisions about its affairs should always come before any international law, court or body.
items.rationale: Absolute sovereigntists (Westphalian, nationalist, anti-imperialist) endorse; names what is overridden so internationalists cannot agree via 'sovereign equality'.

items.text: A person's deepest political loyalty should be to humanity as a whole, ahead of their own country.
items.rationale: Stoic/Kantian cosmopolitans and proletarian internationalists endorse; 'political' keeps religious/family loyalty out; low frame split, acceptable.

items.text: Public decisions should put a country's own people first, even when people in other countries would gain more.
items.rationale: Liberal nationalists and communitarians (special obligations) endorse; agentless; mirror of int-09. Exemplars may evoke aid/trade (glo/mul) — disclosed.

items.text: If a country is outvoted in an international body it has joined, it should be bound by the majority's decision.
items.rationale: Pooled (majority-vote) supranational authority; federalists and committed multilateralists endorse; pairs with int-06; strong frame splitter.

items.text: If an international body makes a decision that most of a country's people oppose, the country should be free to ignore it.
items.rationale: Popular-sovereignty democrats left and right endorse; condition favours the pole; intrinsic dem cross-load disclosed; strong frame splitter.

items.text: Every country should be bound by the laws of a world government on issues that affect everyone, such as climate change or ocean pollution.
items.rationale: World federalists endorse; 'every country' includes one's own so it reads in both frames. Decentralists may reject on fed grounds — disclosed.

items.text: If international bodies mostly serve the interests of the most powerful countries, each country should have the final say over its own affairs.
items.rationale: Post-colonial, anti-imperialist and left sovereigntists endorse, so the pole is not only right-nationalist; condition favours the pole.

items.text: If a choice would help people in other countries more than it would cost a country's own people, that choice should be made.
items.rationale: Impartial cosmopolitans and universalist ethicists endorse; concrete, unloaded stakes replace 'interests vs humanity'; mirror of int-04.

items.text: A person's deepest political loyalty should be to their own country, ahead of any wider global community.
items.rationale: Civic and cultural nationalists and communitarians endorse; 'country' not 'nation' to limit mul cross-load; mirror of int-03.
